thread.title: Apple Earnings and Conference Call: What to Expect and the Potential Reaction

title: Apple Earnings and Conference Call: What to Expect and the Potential Reaction
text:
Apple Earnings and Conference Call: What to Expect and the Potential Reaction By gs
Investors and market watchers will likely be transfixed on Apple's ( AAPL ) quarterly results after Tuesday's market close. Over the last several weeks, there has been a lot of speculation over iPhone X shipments, with several forecast cuts on Wall Street.
The chatter about shipments has only intensified in the last several trading days following comments from Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ) , Samsung and others regarding soft or weak high-end smartphone demand. This led Goldman Sachs ( GS ) to cut its iPhone shipment forecast to 53 million units for the March quarter from 54.7 million. With reports suggesting Apple is looking to burn off some 8 million iPhone units in the current quarter, Goldman and others have also reduced iPhone expectations for the current quarter. Goldman now sees 40.3 million units, down 3.2 million from its prior projection.
Here's the thing, though: Units multiplied by price equal revenue, and in the case of Apple it has several iPhone models, including its newer iPhone 8, that are doing rather well. For both the March-quarter results and Apple's June outlook, the earnings conference call will likely be filled with questions surrounding the average iPhone selling price. Doing the math will help fine tune expectations for overall iPhone units, with a sequential tick down being interpreted as confirmation of falling iPhone X shipments.
Outside of the all-important metrics on iPhones, which account for the bulk of Apple's revenue and profit, odds are we'll see some lift in iPad numbers given the introduction of its latest model that carries a far more affordable price point.
Services will be another key business to watch not only because of its growth trajectory but the recurring nature of several of its offerings, such as Apple Music and iCloud storage. Revenue expectations for that business in the March quarter are running around $8.5 billion, down slightly vs. the December quarter. During the earnings call, we'll be listening to see if Apple reiterates its 2021 goal to have Services hit the $50 billion revenue run rate.
As important as the non-iPhone business may be to the overall Apple story, investors are also focusing on what the company could announce for its capital return program, given its cash balances, tax reform and efforts to repatriate overseas cash. While expectations for iPhone X shipments have been coming down, those for the upsizing of this capital return program are running between $100 billion and $300 billion in the form of dividend increases, share repurchases and acquisitions.
My gut tells me this is likely to be a mixed quarter for Apple with many an investor hoping the upsizing of the capital return program smooths over any near-term iPhone concerns ahead of early June's World Wide Developer Conference. If the market is underwhelmed by the capital return program adjustments, we'll likely see AAPL shares come under pressure. However, with new and likely better prices on iPhones coming later this year and the looming 5G upgrade cycle that could begin in 2019, any near-term pain in the stock could make Apple enticing.
